4. CONSTRUCTION 4.1 The construction of tyre pressure gauges shall be as given in Fig. 1.

shall be suitable to fit on tyre valves 4.2 Connector - The connector having 7.7 V cap threads conforming to `Indian Standard specification for tyre tube valves and accessories ( under preparation )`. When applied to the valves stem, the connector shall depress the valve core plunger permitting the free passage of air from the tyre into the gauge pressure chamber, with no continuous loss of air or damage to the stem or core The connector shall be integral with the body or rigidly members. attached thereto so as not to become loose or detached. 4.3 Dual Connector - The dual connector shall be provided with a dual opposed deflator pin and so constructed as to operate the gauge from one chuck, and render the other chuck deflator pin inoperative. 4.4 Body - The body shall fully shield the internal when the indicating bar is in the closed position. working mechanism

between the indicating bar and 4.5 Indicating Bar - The connection the internal working mechanism shall be such as to permit the indicating bar to remain at the indicated pressure after the source of pressure has been removed. The graduation marks and figures shall be stamped or etched to be permanent and legible. The indicating bar shall protrude sufficiently beyond the maximum readin g to show that the tyre pressure gauge is subjected to excessive pressure. 4.6 The design and construction of the gauge shall be such of the indicating bar does not alter the calibration. 4.7 Subject to agreement between the 4 purchaser and that rotation the

8.1 The visual inspection of the surface of the tyre pressure reveal no injurious defects, such as cracks, and'unevenness. scales shall be marked lcgihly and indelibly. 9. TESTS

9.1 Accuracy Test - This test is carried out with the help of an air accumulator which is able to regulate air pressure by an air compressor valve. Accuracy shall be established against and pressure regulating test gauge conforming to IS : 3624-1966*. The pressure shall be regulated to the maximum and at three suitable points of scale ( one of the points being the most often used pressure and the other maximum pressure ). The indicator error shall be read in the upward, downward and horizontal positions. The tyrc pressure gauge shall meet the following requirements: a) The error indicatccl shall be within f 1 scale division corresponding to the minimum scale unit given in 3.1, b) The movement c) There of indicator shall be smooth, and of value

shall be no air leakage

at any part of the gauge.

9.2 Durability Test - The tyre operations with six operations per three-fourths of the maximum requirements specified in 9.1 after

pressure gauge shall be tested for 1 000 minute speed under an air pressure of scale. The gauge shall meet all the this test.

9.3 Overload Test -The pressure gauge shall be subjected to 25 percent overload pressure for 10 minutes continuously.. The gauge shall then be subjected to the accuracy test and shall meet all the requirements given under 9.1. 9.4 Shock Test - The gauge shnll br capable of withstanding shock without dlm?,ge when dropped frrcly from a height of one metre on to a concrete surface three times, once with the connector downwards and the bar cxtcnded, once with the connector upwards and the bar extended and once with the connector horizontal and the bar extended. The gaugz shall be then subjected to the accuracy test given in 9.1 and shall meet the requirements accordingly. without 9.5 Storage Test - The gauges shall be able to withstand dam-lge, storage in the temperature of - 10 to 43�C. Following these rxp?sures for sufficient duration and after being stabilized at a temperature of 27 f 2"C, the gauges shall be capable of meeting the requirements of the accuracy trst as given in 9.1.

NOTE - The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Rcgulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further aafeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution,

11. PACKING
II.1 Each gauge shall be packed in a wooden box, with adequate cushioning material to minimize movement of the gauge and to ensure that the gauge is capable of withstandin g normal transit risks without damage. The packing shall be made in such a manner as to prevent the interior mechanism or the connector becoming exposed to contamination by foreign matter likely to affect the accuracy of the gauge.
